summary: Tested the SEO, security and performance changes on backend and frontend. Backend: 15 of 16 tests pass in /app/backend/tests/test_security_seo.py. Passing: security headers (nosniff, DENY, Referrer-Policy, HSTS) on public API responses; Cache-Control no-store on /api/auth/*; CORS allows sunjayaasia.com, www and the preview origin and rejects evil.com on GET and preflight; brute-force lockout (5x401 then 429 with the exact message, also for the upper-case email); real superadmin login plus /auth/me; robots.txt is text/plain and sitemap.xml is text/xml with all 7 sunjayaasia.com URLs; index.html has Organization and WebSite JSON-LD. The one failure is a real security gap: the lockout can be bypassed by sending a fake X-Forwarded-For header. Frontend: every route (/, /about, /pillars, /subsidiaries, /news, /contact, /legal) sets its own title, description, canonical, og:url and og:title, each tag appears only once, and a trailing slash is normalised. /admin gets 'noindex, nofollow' and the title 'CMS — Sunjaya Asia Group'. All 5 Google font families load and no images are broken. The only console errors were the expected 401/429 responses from the lockout test. The /admin UI shows the toast 'Too many failed attempts. Try again in 15 minute(s).' on the 6th try with a fake email. The real admin login works (1 attempt, no failures on real accounts), and the Images and Content tabs load. A no-op PUT /api/content/{id} with the same value returned 200 and the value was unchanged.

critical.issue: Lockout bypass: _client_ip() takes the FIRST value of X-Forwarded-For, which the client controls. After 5 failures (429 lock), the next request with 'X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4' gets 401 again instead of 429. So an attacker can rotate the header and guess passwords without limit. Fix: take the right-most / trusted-proxy hop (e.g. split(',')[-1], or X-Real-IP from the ingress). Better still, also keep a per-email counter that does not depend on IP.

minor.issue: _seed_superadmin_if_empty() runs an extra Supabase SELECT on every login. Seeding also only happens when the table is empty, so if SUPER_ADMIN_PASSWORD changes in env the existing admin is not updated (playbook check 5).
JWT is stored in localStorage as a Bearer token, not an httpOnly cookie (playbook check 2 not applicable). This is acceptable given the CORS allow-list, but an XSS could steal the token.

issues: Duplicate preconnect tags for fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com (lines ~22-23 and ~32-33). Harmless but redundant.
A separate legacy Inter:wght@600 stylesheet link is still loaded alongside the main font link, an extra render-blocking request. Merge it into the main css2 URL if Inter is still used.

action_items: HIGH: Fix _client_ip in server.py so a spoofed X-Forwarded-For cannot bypass the login lockout (use the trusted right-most hop or X-Real-IP, and/or add a per-email failure counter)
Optional: remove the duplicate preconnect links in index.html and fold the Inter stylesheet into the main Google Fonts link
Optional: stop running _seed_superadmin_if_empty on every login (do it once at startup)
critical_code_review_comments: _client_ip trusts client-controlled XFF[0]: this is the lockout bypass above
Lockout only counts failures per ip:email pair, so attempts spread across many IPs against one email are never locked. Consider a per-email threshold too.
RouteSeo: unknown routes fall back to the home title and description but get their own canonical URL. Consider noindex for 404 paths.
The security headers middleware and CORS config look correct. Cache-Control no-store is applied to /api/auth and /api/admin.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Rerun test_security_seo.py; test_xff_spoof_bypass should pass after the fix. The preview host is behind Cloudflare: many rapid page.goto calls trigger a bot challenge with 429 responses. Use SPA navigation with history.pushState plus a popstate event to visit routes inside one page load.
rca of the issue: server.py _client_ip(): fwd.split(',')[0] returns whatever the client sent first in X-Forwarded-For, because the ingress appends the real IP after it. The ident becomes '<spoofed>:email', which is a new lock bucket. Reproduce: 5 bad logins with a fake email, then a 6th with the header 'X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4' returns 401 instead of 429. Mitigation: use the last hop or a trusted header, and add a per-email counter.
